text: Decision cards, third approach. Two tries rewrote proposal titles into questions with word-replacement code; both were rejected (a loop that hangs the site build, garbled questions). Plain-language questions need a model, not string rules. Instead: when the steward raises a proposal above its limit, it also writes five short fields into the work-item record: question (one yes/no line in plain words), if_yes, if_no, cost, recommendation with a one-line reason. The decisions page renders those fields first and puts evidence paths in a collapsed section. A proposal without the fields shows its title and 'No brief written yet'. No text transformation code in the site build. Acceptance: a test that a steward proposal record with the five fields renders them before any path; a test that a record without them renders 'No brief written yet'; the steward role prompt states the five fields and the owner-style rules (short, plain, no jargon).
